cases.target_stage: Original merits judgment in RC ARC No. 845/19 on the Section 14(1)(b) eviction petition, pronounced 30.03.2026
cases.target_court: Additional Rent Controller-01 (Central), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
cases.substantive_issue: Whether the legal heirs of Rawat Mal Saini sublet, assigned, or parted with possession of the tenanted premises to M/s Divya Jyoti Electronics, placing respondent no.2 in exclusive possession without written landlord consent.

issue_refs.quote: The other requirement required to be proved is that the tenant has either: Sub-let the premises, or assigned his tenancy rights, or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or part of the premises.

application_refs.quote: the pleadings and evidence led by the petitioner regarding the existence of tenancy in the name of Rawat Mal Saini and the subsequent parting with possession in favour of respondent no.2 remain uncontroverted.
was in exclusive possession of the premises and the LRs of respondent no.1 was no longer in possession of the demised premises.

In the absence of any material to show that the landlord had consented to respondent no.2's occupation, or that the LRs of respondent no.1 continued to exercise any control or supervision over the premises, the inference that the tenant had parted with possession in favour of respondent no.2 is irresistible.

the petitioner has been successful in establishing that the respondent no.2 was running his own separate business from the suit premises. This fact is sufficient in itself that the legal as well as physical possession of the suit premises was conveyed to the respondent no.2.

Though the LRs of respondent no.1 claim to be in possession of the suit premises but the same stands unproved. Consequently, the essential ingredients of cite8†Section 14 (1) (b) DRC Act stand satisfied.

allowed_spans.reason: Respondents' express denial of the pleaded absence of possession and unauthorized transfer.

independent_rule_leads.quote: It is well settled that the burden of proving subletting is on the landlord but if the landlord proves that the subtenant is in exclusive possession of the suit premises, then the onus is shifted to the tenant to prove that it was not a case of subletting.
The word 'subletting' necessarily means transfer of an exclusive right to enjoy the property in favour of the third party.

cases.target_stage: Original merits judgment in E. No. 385/06/04 on the Section 14(1)(b) eviction petition, decided 20.11.2010
cases.target_court: Additional Rent Controller, North-West, Rohini, Delhi
cases.substantive_issue: Whether operation of M/s Balaji Enterprises from the tenanted premises amounted to subletting or parting with possession, where respondent no.1 asserted that he was the sole proprietor of both the original and later business concerns.

issue_refs.quote: In the present case it is stated by petitioner that the premises was let out to the respondent no.1 who has let out/ parted with possession to the respondent no.2. The respondent has raised the defence that he is the sole proprietor of M/s Balaji Enterprises respondent no.2.

application_refs.quote: The respondent no.2 is the sole proprietorship firm for which the respondent no.1 is the proprietor.

Therefore, on the basis of the evidence, it is clear that the respondent no.2 is the sole proprietorship concern of respondent no.1 who is the tenant of the suit premises. Even after creation of new firm possession of the tenanted premises is with the original tenant. Therefore, it cannot be said that it is the case of subletting or parting with possession without consent of the landlord.

Moreover, even after creation of the second partnership firm the possession is with the original tenant. Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that petitioner is not able to prove the necessary ingredients of cite8†section 14(1)(b) of DRC Act , hence petition is dismissed.

excluded_stage_notes: The ownership/acquisition, roof-damage, joinder, and joint-tenancy defenses are outside the selected substantive issue.
The reference to an earlier Section 14(1)(a) proceeding in cross-examination is not treated as part of the selected Section 14(1)(b) application.

independent_rule_leads.quote: A firm unless expressly provided for the purpose of any statute is not a legal entity.
Where the old and new firms have a common partner the occupation will be by one of the original tenants.
the possession of the tenanted shop remain with the tenant during and after dissolution of partnership, therefore, the case of subletting is not made out.

coverage_gaps: The target court does not separately adjudicate written consent after finding that possession remained with the original tenant; that condition should be masked rather than assigned a separate factual label.

IK-69998629:L121 refers to a 'second partnership firm' although the record and the preceding application describe respondent no.2 as a sole proprietorship; the source wording is preserved without reconciliation.

cases.target_stage: Original merits judgment in E. No. 2/2011 on the Section 14(1)(b) eviction application, decided 26.10.2013
cases.target_court: Rent Controller, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
cases.substantive_issue: Whether M/s Gill & Co. had been reconstituted so that the original partners were displaced and Ramesh Tiwari/Rajan Tiwari obtained exclusive possession, amounting to subletting or parting with possession.

issue_refs.quote: The next question to be considered for determination as to whether the premises have been sub­let or its possession has been parted with by the respondent in view of change in the constitution of the partnership firm, M/s Gill & Co.

application_refs.quote: there is no such admission, specific or categorical as claimed by the petitioners.

Further the relevant documents from the Registrar of Firms, i.e. registration certificate, Form A containing the names of the partners as well as the original partnership deed are sufficient to prove that Mr Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Ashok Kumar Bhasin are also the partners of M/s Gill & Co alongwith Mr. Ramesh Tiwari and Rajan Tiwari till today.

In this case, in view of the pleadings as well as the testimony of the witnesses and the documents on record, it is proved that the respondent firm consisted of four partners before inception of tenancy till filing of this petition.

The petitioners have categorically failed to prove either any change in the constitution of the firm or exclusive possession by the partners Ramesh Tiwari and Rajan Tiwari to the exclusion of earlier partners Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Ashok Kumar Bhasin.

this court is of the opinion that the petitioners have categorically failed to prove that the premises have been sublet or its possession has been parted with by the respondent without obtaining the consent of the landlord in writing.

allowed_spans.quote: It is averred that none of the partners of the respondent who constituted the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co at the time of inception of tenancy are now the partner of the respondent no. 1 and none of the said partners is in actual possession or legal possession of the tenanted premises.
allowed_spans.reason: Petitioners' pleaded factual theory of displacement of the original partners.

allowed_spans.quote: tenanted premises to Sh. Ramesh Tewari and Sh Rajan Tewari, who constituted M/s Gill & Co and are in occupation of the entire shop.
allowed_spans.reason: Petitioners' pleaded account of occupation by the alleged new partners.

allowed_spans.quote: It is stated that change in constitution of partnership firm does not amount to change in tenancy and even otherwise the respondent firm still consists of partners who had taken the premises in question on rent.
allowed_spans.reason: Respondent's written-statement denial of a displacing reconstitution.

allowed_spans.quote: Rajan Tiwari was one of the partners at the commencement of tenancy on 19.8.1991; that the premises were let out to the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co and not to any individual partners in his individual capacity as tenant and the possession of the tenanted premises is still with the firm, i.e. M/s Gill & Co.
allowed_spans.reason: Respondent's affirmative account of original partnership membership and continuing firm possession.

allowed_spans.quote: at present, none of the partners, who were the partners of M/s Gill & Co at he time of inception of tenancy, are now the partners of the entity and the earlier partners have illegally sublet, assigned and parted with possession of the tenanted premises to some new partners
allowed_spans.reason: PW1's evidentiary restatement of the alleged replacement of the original partners.

allowed_spans.quote: the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co which consisted of four partners as mentioned in the partnership deed dated 17.8.1991 Ex. RW1A. The witness proved the Forms A and B issued by the office of Registrar of Firms as Ex. RW1/F and RW1/G.
allowed_spans.reason: RW1 evidence identifying the partnership deed and Registrar of Firms records supporting four partners.

allowed_spans.quote: The witness has proved the account opening form, undertaking and letter of partnership all dated 5.12.1991 as Ex. RW1/B1 to B3
allowed_spans.reason: Additional contemporaneous partnership/bank documents introduced by RW1.

excluded_stage_notes: The landlord-tenant relationship is expressly treated as admitted at IK-84524189:L163-L164 and is not the selected substantive issue.
Site-plan, ownership succession, and rent-payment background are not used as target-condition application spans.

independent_rule_leads.quote: that the tenant has, on or after the 9 day of June, 1952, sublet, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;
the onus to prove subletting is on the landlord and if he establishes parting of with the possession in favour of a third party, the onus would shift to the tenant to explain his possession.
User by other person is not parting with possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself.

coverage_gaps: The underlying Registrar of Firms and partnership exhibits are summarized but not reproduced in full in the rendering.

The dispositive reasoning rests on failure to prove change in constitution/exclusive possession; written consent is not separately supported by an affirmative factual finding and should not be independently labeled.
